chapters.title: Getting Started
chapters.blurb: Understanding programming, Python fundamentals, and leaving garden notes.

lessons.title: What is Programming?
goals: Understand that programs follow instructions step by step
Display your first instruction: Step 1: Plant seed
lessons.starter_code:
# Computers follow instructions step by step
print("Step 1: Plant seed")

rules.hint: Put your text inside quotes: print("Step 1: Plant seed")

lessons.title: What is Python?
goals: Learn that Python runs code from top to bottom
Make the console say: Python is ready!
lessons.starter_code:
# Python is case-sensitive! Always use lowercase print()
print("Python is ready!")

rules.hint: Remember lowercase print: print("Python is ready!")

lessons.title: Leaving Garden Notes
goals: Use the # symbol to write a comment that Python ignores
Keep the message line active to print: Notes are free
lessons.starter_code:
# Add a # in front of this note so Python ignores it
# Plant seeds carefully
print("Notes are free")

rules.hint: Lines starting with # are notes for you. Python only runs lines without #

chapters.title: First Sprouts
chapters.blurb: Displaying output, variables, plant labels, and math calculations.

lessons.title: Say Hello
goals: Use print() to say hello to your garden
Make the console say exactly: Hello, garden!
lessons.starter_code:
# Say hello to your garden
print("Hello, garden!")

rules.hint: Text goes inside quotes: print("Hello, garden!")

lessons.title: Name Your Water
goals: Create a variable named water and set it to 4
Print the variable's value using print(water)
lessons.starter_code:
# Store a number in a variable, then print it
water = 4
print(water)

rules.hint: A variable stores a value: water = 4. Print it without quotes: print(water)

lessons.title: Label Your Plant
goals: Store the plant name "Sunflower" in the crop variable
Print the plant label to the console
lessons.starter_code:
# Label your plant with a text string
crop = "Sunflower"
print(crop)

rules.hint: Words go inside quotation marks: crop = "Sunflower"

lessons.title: Count the Seeds
goals: Multiply seeds by pots using *
Print the total seeds needed (18)
lessons.starter_code:
seeds = 6
pots = 3
# Multiply seeds by pots and print total
print(seeds * pots)

rules.hint: Python uses * for multiplication: print(seeds * pots)

chapters.title: Growing Logic
chapters.blurb: Making decisions with conditionals, repeating with loops, and organizing lists.

lessons.title: Sunny or Not?
goals: Write an if that checks if sun > 5
Add an else block for when sunlight is low
Print Grow! when the sun is bright

rules.hint: End the if and else lines with a colon (:) and indent the print lines by 4 spaces.

lessons.title: Water Every Plant
goals: Use a for loop with range(3)
Print Water plant 1, Water plant 2, and Water plant 3
lessons.expected_output:
Water plant 1
Water plant 2
Water plant 3

rules.hint: range(3) counts 0, 1, 2. Use i + 1 to display 1, 2, 3!

lessons.title: Seed Basket
goals: Create a list of 3 plants with square brackets [ ]
Access and print the second plant using [1]
Make the console display: Mint
lessons.starter_code:
# Store 3 garden plants in a list
basket = ["Rose", "Mint", "Fern"]
# Print the second plant (index 1)
print(basket[1])

rules.hint: Python starts counting at index 0! So basket[0] is Rose, and basket[1] is Mint.
